subject: SLA draft: batched-inference latency carveout & monthly credit structure
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Park <emily@nubisys.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-02T09:21:00-07:00
Subject: SLA draft and a couple questions on batched inference

Hi Emily —

Thanks for the time on the call earlier. Attached is a first-pass SLA we put together based on our standard hosted offering and the notes from today (attachment: Redwood_SLA_Draft_v1.pdf). A few things to call out up front so you can focus review: 

- Baseline availability: 99.95% monthly for hosted API endpoints.
- Standard latency commitment: p95 <= 300ms for single-request (non-batched) paths.
- Batched inference: we flagged this as a potential exception path since batching trades latency for throughput. Proposed carveout: p95 <= 500ms for batched routes with a separate monthly remedy schedule.
- Remedy (credits): proportional monthly credit formula rather than fixed % tiers — proposal included in section 4.
- Maintenance windows: we include a 4-hour/month maintenance allowance as carveout.

Two asks from our side as you review:
1) Can you confirm which Nimbus routes must remain single-request low-latency (i.e., cannot accept batched behavior)?
2) Would Nimbus prefer a stricter uptime (99.99%) for any given route if you were willing to shift that route to Dedicated capacity (we can price that separately)?

If you want, Ben and Laura are copied to help scope commercial and credit mechanics. If this looks broadly sensible, we can iter on credit caps and a short pilot window (30–90 days) so you can validate behavior against your traffic.

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachment: Redwood_SLA_Draft_v1.pdf

From: Emily Park <emily@nubisys.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-03T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SLA draft and a couple questions on batched inference

Vivek —

Thanks for sending this over. I shared the draft with our reliability and legal teams; a few immediate concerns to flag: 

- Nimbus's production-critical endpoints require 99.99% availability (monthly) — 99.95 won't be acceptable for those without contractual exceptions.
- Batched inference is fine for analytics/backfill routes, but we cannot allow best-effort latency on customer-facing real-time routes. We need per-route SLOs documented in the contract.
- Credits: your proportional formula is conceptually OK, but the cap and timing are important. Nimbus legal pushed back on anything that limits total monthly credits to less than 50% of billed service for production endpoints.
- We also need historical uptime and month-by-month p95 latency reports for the last 12 months for the specific models/endpoints we will use. Legal will want that before signing.

I'm attaching our internal requirements doc so you can map the ask to the draft (attachment: Nimbus_SLA_Reqs.docx).

Looking forward to a follow-up — can you loop in someone on the reliability side if we need deeper telemetry?

—Emily
Emily Park
Head of Platform Reliability
Nimbus Systems

Attachment: Nimbus_SLA_Reqs.docx

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-04T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Nimbus comments on SLA draft — need guidance on credits / carveouts

Forwarding Nimbus feedback — highlights below and a couple questions for commercial/legal input: 

Emily says: 99.99% for production-critical, per-route SLOs required, and wants 12 months of uptime/latency history. Legal asked for a cap of no less than 50% credits for production endpoints (they see that as a non-starter to limit).

Draft options I'm considering to keep this mutually acceptable while limiting downside:
- Option A (default hosted): keep 99.95 baseline for hosted; offer per-route SLAs for specific endpoints with a premium and commitment to move to Dedicated for 99.99.
- Option B (batched carveout): allow batched inference routes but require Nimbus to tag them as "best-effort" in the contract; specify p95 <= 500ms for batched routes, with a separate credit ladder (higher cap for batched).
- Credits: propose an introductory cap of 30% of monthly bill for the first 90 days of production, stepping to 20% thereafter, for batched carveouts. For dedicated/production routes we can accept a higher cap but only if they pay for Dedicated capacity.

Questions:
1) Ben — are we comfortable with 30% first-quarter cap as a public offer?
2) Laura — can we provide the 12-month telemetry report without jumping the fence on data disclosure? If so, what format is safe to send (aggregated p95 by calendar month)?

I'll draft a follow-up that shows a clean Option A/B comparison for Emily.

-Vivek

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-05T13:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Nimbus comments on SLA draft — need guidance on credits / carveouts

Vivek —

30% cap for the first 90 days (then 20%) on batched carveouts seems defendable as a pilot concession; it gives Nimbus runway while limiting our exposure. A couple additional negotiation levers: 

- Offer a per-route add-on: 99.99 SLA on Dedicated for an uplift (we should give a price band and lead time).
- For hosted production routes: keep 99.95 baseline but allow a negotiated exception to 99.99 only if they purchase a reliability add-on and sign a 12-month commit.
- Credits: cap credits at 50% only for Dedicated production endpoints where they pay the uplift. For hosted endpoints the cap should be <= 30% (intro) / 20% (steady-state).

Operational asks to include in the contract: monthly health report (aggregated availability and p95), access to incident timelines within 24 hours, and a playbook for batched fallback behavior (how we degrade). Those will reduce legal friction.

I'll attach the credit matrix I used for prior negotiations so you can reference numbers when we present (attachment: sla-credit-matrix.xlsx).

—Ben

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-07T16:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Nimbus comments on SLA draft — need guidance on credits / carveouts

Quick operational/legal guidance: 

1) Telemetry: we can share 12 months of aggregated monthly availability and p95 latency by endpoint (no raw logs). Provide it as a CSV with month, availability %, p95 latency, requests. That satisfies their ask without exposing identifiable customer data.

2) Ramp clause: include a 90-day onboarding ramp for new production routes. During ramp we apply an elevated remedy cap (30%) to protect the customer while we tune performance; after 90 days it moves to standard cap (20%) unless they select Dedicated.

3) Batched carveout language: define a "batched route" precisely (batch window, expected throughput, and labeling requirement). Contract should require Nimbus to explicitly designate which route IDs are batched. If they later convert a batched route to real-time production, the higher SLA (and price) must be applied with 30 days' notice.

4) Credits: accept Ben's approach — Dedicated buys higher availability and higher credit cap; hosted production capped lower.

I'll incorporate these items into an updated draft. Once we have Nimbus agreement on structure, send the final via DocuSign (link prepared: https://na3.docusign.net/Signing/?acct=1234xxxx&env=prod).

Laura Bennett
Director, Contracts & Partnerships
Redwood Inference
